Then, $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{AB}}=\overrightarrow{\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{A}}-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}$ \begin{aligned} & \left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{AB}}\right|=\sqrt{25^2+25^2} \\ & =25 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr} \end{aligned} From diagram, we can clearly see when A reaches point ' $\mathrm{C}$ ' its distance is closest from $\mathrm{B}$. \tan \theta=\frac{\left|\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}\right|}{\left|\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{A}}\right|}=1 \Rightarrow \theta=45^{\circ} So, $\mathrm{AC}=50 \cos 45^{\circ}=25 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~km}$ Then, $\mathrm{t}=\frac{\mathrm{AC}}{\left|\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{AB}}\right|}=\frac{25 \sqrt{2}}{25 \sqrt{2}}=1 \mathrm{hr}=60 \mathrm{~min}$

To complete vertical circle, minimum velocity should be $\sqrt{5 \mathrm{Rg}}$, where $\mathrm{R}=$ Radius of circle
